Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

ethnic adjective

also ethnically, ethnic group, ethnic origin, ethnicity, by descent

classical

Gell. 17.8.4: aetātis et gentis argūtiīs

gentis

the genitive of gēns, beside the noun it describes; gentium of several peoples · Wiktionary

of a people: ethnic

Latin has no adjective for “ethnic”: it uses the people itself, gēns (see international), in the genitive, or the people’s own name (Graecus, Thrāx). An ethnic group is simply a gēns or a nātiō.

Other words

  • genere — by descent, ethnically

    the ablative of genus, with an adjective of nationality · also used · classical · Gell. 17.8.4: puer genere Atticus; Caes. BG 4.12.4: amplissimō genere nātus (Lewis & Short, s.v. genus) · Wiktionary

    Birth, descent: genere Atticus, Athenian by birth; also of family rank (nōbilī genere nātus).

  • stirps, stirpis f. — stock, lineage, descent

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 70: ignōrātiō stirpis et generis (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. minority (ethnic, religious, etc.): minor dīversae stirpis plēbs (Egger) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Literally the stock of a plant; of people, a family line. Egger’s ethnic minority is “people of a different stock”.

  • ethnicus, ethnica, ethnicum — heathen, pagan

    avoid · late Latin · Tert. Pud. 9; Vulg. Mt. 5.47 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    A false friend: in Latin, from Greek ἐθνικός, it means a heathen, a gentile (Tertullian, the Vulgate), not “ethnic”.

Examples

  • erat is puer genere Atticus, ad annōs maximē nātus octō, fēstīvissimīs aetātis et gentis argūtiīs scatēns

    the boy was an Athenian by birth, eight years old at most, bubbling over with all the wit of his age and of his peopleGell. 17.8.4

See also minority, international, national, foreign.
